full_judgment: Mr Sohrab Hossain, the learned advocate appearing on behalf of the complainant opposite-party No. 2 submitted that the petition of complaint may not disclose a prima facie case under section 406 of the Penal Code but the facts and circumstances as stated therein disclose an offence under section 420 of the Penal Code and, as such, the learned Magistrate has rightly issued the processes against the petitioners. He further submitted that the petition of complaint discloses a criminal offence inasmuch as, the petitioners in the face of the delivery order passed by the Senior Export Officer accused Md Ayub disobeyed the order in not delivering the goods for making wrongful gain for themselves. Hr further submitted that the pay order No. 360757 dated 22-9-77 Janata Bank (Imamganj, Dacca) having been given to the petitioners on 22-9-77 they sat over the pay order for long three months with an ulterior motive to cause wrongful lose to the complainant. Mr Shahid Alam, the learned advocate appearing for the state supported the arguments advanced by Mr Sohrab Hossain. The learned advocate for the state submitted that the prosecution should not be stifled at the initial stage without taking further evidence in the case and that the application for quashing is premature.
